newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends near yr-high on steady FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends near yr-high on steady FOMC.

text.p: The Mexican peso ended trade on Tuesday close to its firmest levels for the year shortly after the Federal Open Market Committee left U.S. interest rate policy unchanged.
"It's more good news for the peso," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.9 and
1.05 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7550/7.7570 and 7.7510/7.7625 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso reached its strongest closing rate of the year, at 7.7450 per dollar, on February 20.
Same-day peso contracts had closed trade mid-morning 2.1 centavos firmer at 7.7500/7.7530 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso could gain further strength on Wednesday if domestic interest rates were to increase in line with market forecasts.

A Reuters poll of nine money market traders showed they forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at 19.06 percent, which would be a gain of 35 basis points from last week's auction.
